They are all in this — not all, probably there’s some people in the SaaS sales department who are just kind of there for the paycheck — but a lot of the key people at these companies are united in their belief that they are building [AGI].One person, I won’t say who, but one person at one of these companies recently told me that they think their company might be the last company. I thought, “The last company to IPO this year? What do you mean?” They were like, “No, we think this might be the teleological end of capitalism and there might never be another large company primarily run by humans.”So these people are weird, and weird in ways that are worrying, but also very interesting. This is what I was trying to do in the book. I didn’t want to tell you that these people are terrible or great. It’s just that you need to know who they are. You need to know that they all hate each other. You need to know that they are this peculiar breed of thinkers to understand the dynamics of the race.There’s a portion of your book where you talk about people splitting away from effective altruism to go become accelerationists, and you have a woman in there who’s like, “Well, the accelerationists have better parties, and I like those vibes better.” I thought to myself, “Well, what does that have to do with potentially killing everyone?”But they are very human, even though they’re trying to build something that might ultimately dehumanize us all in various ways. What did you make of that as you were doing all this reporting?The notion that there’s existential risk here looms over the book, it looms over the industry. Every time we do an episode on it, the audience is like, “Why won’t they just stop?” Bill Gates was just on Decoder and said, “You could just stop if you were the only company. If you thought you were going to be the only company with AGI, then OpenAI’s model would work. But the second there are more frontier companies, it absolutely won’t work. By the way, they might kill you all.” I thought to myself, “Well, Bill Gates is not very optimistic right at this moment in time.”No, he is not.What do you make of that — that they are racing ahead even though they know the risks are huge in the absence of any regulatory authority that could cause any of them to solve these problems?I think there are probably two or three reasons that they’re doing it. I’ve asked them all pretty much. I talked to 150 or so people for my book and I asked all of them some version of this: “If it’s so dangerous, why are you doing it?” The answers would usually start with some fatalistic… I don’t know, you could call it inevitabilism. They were just like, “Look, someone is going to build this. The recipe is not that hard. All you need is a bunch of compute and a bunch of data and the right algorithms, and you get AGI. And so if it is possible, it will happen and it would be good for us to do it rather than people we don’t think are as trustworthy.” That is sort of reason number one, the harm reduction argument.Then there are the true believers who say, “This is all going to turn out great, so long as we thread the needle, and if we can build this stuff without blowing up humanity, wrecking the entire internet, or developing novel bioweapons.”Technology is usually a force for good throughout history. I don’t think a lot of people would switch lives with their great-great-grandparents. It sucked to be a subsistence farmer. I think there are people who believe that we are the equivalent of subsistence farmers today, and that what is coming will be so great that we will want to live in that world.And then there are just people who are like, “Look, this is fun and I like doing it, and it’s fun to make the neural networks code. And so that’s what we’re going to keep doing.”That aspect of it where every now and again I look up and I’m like, well, my computer just did something that I’ve never seen a computer do before, is fun.It’s awesome.It is. It’s legitimately fun. It’s some of the most fun I think you can have with a computer ever. Then I’m always led to think about, “Well, this came at some massive cost. I might be empowering some corporation that ultimately wants to kill us all.” Somewhere in there is the swirl of all the tech CEOs standing behind Donald Trump in the Oval Office to do something, to sign some sort of morally binding AI safety pledge. And all that feels very conflicted.I would put that in the category of AI backlash. We hear the AI companies talk about, “Well, the technology just hasn’t diffused enough. People haven’t seen the benefits, so they naturally hate change. We have a marketing problem. We just need to communicate about it more.”Is that just the prevailing view as you talk to these folks, that eventually the stuff will speak for itself, or do you think they’ve internalized that there’s more of a backlash?I don’t think they’re surprised by the backlash. I don’t think they like it. They wish it weren’t happening. But I was talking to one CEO at one of these companies who said, “Yeah, I get it. We haven’t cured any diseases yet. Yes, we think our tools are capable of doing interesting things, but we don’t have a lot of things on the scoreboard in the big societal improvements category yet.”I think there are some people in the industry who lament the fact that the chatbots came before the cancer cures and wish that they could have figured out a way to do it in the other order. It’s just that that is kind of the way the tech tree grew.So they feel like now the only responsible thing to do is keep pushing on the cancer cures so that when people look at what has AI done to our lives, it’s like, “Well, yes, it helps my kid cheat on their homework and they’re addicted to an AI companion, but also my grandma is still alive and she wouldn’t have been if this medicine had not been discovered by AI.”Yeah, there’s some dynamic in there that brings me back to Google, I think as this conversation has done many times, where your reporting on Google’s approach to AI was that this is just task-based software. “We’re going to make Google Search 10 percent better, Gmail will be 5 percent better, and we will continually deploy these improvements, and no one else has our access to data or our scale, and thus we’ll be fine.”OpenAI shows up and it puts itself in Bing. Famously, Bing tries to make out with you. Still my all-time favorite… I can’t believe I haven’t brought this up yet. This is my all-time favorite story.I can’t believe you haven’t brought it up either. I had an over-under bet going on how long it would take you, and I took the under in a minute.[Laughs] Well, you and I have already talked about it in our lives. I was like, “I’ve got all these other deep questions.” But yeah, Bing is famously horny for my friend Kevin Roose. That moment I think just galvanized people: “Wow, these things can do a lot of things.”Google had to react, and they didn’t react by going all in. They sort of stutter-stepped there. As you’ve been saying, they’re still not all the way there. Google still doesn’t think this thing is going to happen. They think they’re making better Google products for people.When I look at the trial transcripts from Musk v. Altman about the founding of OpenAI, they’re all terrified of Google.Yes.They’re all terrified of Demis Hassabis at Google, specifically, doing the thing, just making it happen because he has the resources. I can’t tell if they were right or wrong about that.I think they were right to be taking note of how DeepMind was doing. I mean, if you take yourself back in time to 2015 or 2016, DeepMind was the only sort of AGI lab of any real importance. They were beating Go, they were beating other games, they were beating StarCraft. They were really cooking using this sort of method of reinforcement learning, deep reinforcement learning.There were people who thought that was the thing that was going to scale all the way to AGI. There were people who thought AlphaGo was the path, because if a system could go from never having played Go before to beating the world’s best humans at Go in the span of a few hours as AlphaGo Zero did, then maybe you could just replace Go with any arbitrary thing — math or coding or something — and you could climb the ladder very quickly on those tasks.Now, it turned out that didn’t work, at least not without the LLM. But I think people had very real and reasonable fears that that would work. In an alternate universe where it had, I think DeepMind would’ve gotten to AGI first because they were so far ahead of the competition.Are there other paths? Is it just next-token prediction? Is it just LLMs? Or are there other paths that might get you to AGI?I mean, there are other paths that might. I think people who are skeptical of LLMs often fall back on this world model idea. I don’t place a lot of stock in that. But there are people who think that to achieve AGI, you need to be able to visually understand the physical world and drive a robot and things.I’m kind of a believer that it’s all software. So I think that LLMs are the most promising path yet. Now, maybe you need to make some tweaks to the architecture. Maybe you need to build in continual learning methods. Maybe it’s not just literally scaling up the same transformer-based LLMs that we’ve had for the past six or seven years. But it sure seems like it is continuing to work, and I think all of the labs are betting that it will continue to work forever.All right. Now I am going to ask you about Bing and Sydney.Please.Obviously, I’ve been thinking about it a lot. I can’t stop talking about it. It’s my favorite thing to talk about.First question, am I still married to a human woman?Are you still married to a human being?Yes.I just remember that period, in 2023, when four different people woke up one day and said, “The computers are alive.” Or they had some out-of-body experience with a chatbot. You were one of them. Ben Thompson was one of them. Blake Lemoine at Google was one of them.A lot of different people said, “It’s obviously alive. I’m having this completely insane experience with a computer. No computer’s ever talked to me this way before.” Sydney in particular was like, “Break up with your wife,” it sent you heart emojis. It’s very good. I encourage everyone to go read that Times article, which by the way, also credit to The Times for thinking, “This should be on the front page of The New York Times.” Incredible editorial insight there to immediately put that on the front page.I don’t think you feel that way about chatbots anymore. I think most people have come to recognize that the computers are not alive. There’s something that happened where if you gave the people in 2026 a 2023-class chatbot and asked, “Do you think this is alive?” I think maybe not everyone in the world, but some enormous set of people has now had enough experiences to respond, “Well, this is pretty dumb and it’s hallucinating.” I’m just wondering how you place that in the context of AGI.So first of all, a slight correction. I never said Sydney was alive. In fact, I said explicitly that I didn’t think Sydney was alive, and that I understood that this was not a sentient AI system. So I’m not sure my own judgment has wavered on that point.In fact, I would probably put a higher p(consciousness) on today’s AI systems than I would on the models of 2023. But I understand what you’re saying, obviously. I think there was a moment for a lot of us, and I think it was GPT-4 for most people.[Laughs] I’m sorry, let me correct. There’s a reason I think this. One of the headlines was “Bing’s AI chat: ‘I want to be alive.’”Yes. It said it wanted to be alive.This is why I have the word alive in my head.The body of the story makes clear that I did not buy that it was alive.But that’s why it’s in my head is that that was the headline in The New York Times.Headlines are so powerful, Nilay.[Laughs] Yes. They framed my own thinking. I’m nothing but a next-token prediction machine.[Laughs] But you’re a very sophisticated one. You’re like a GPT-7-class model.Oh, I’m there. Yeah, obviously.Look, I have come to think that there’s a very banal explanation for why Sydney was so compelling and creepy, which was that it was the first public deployment of GPT-4. We did not know it at the time. But that was GPT-4, an early sort of not fully post-trained version of GPT-4 that Microsoft had jumped the gun and shoved into Bing before it was ready. But that was GPT-4.I think there actually was a subjective step change in what it was like to talk to a GPT-4-class model versus a GPT-3-class model. Maybe it was just that it passed the Turing test at GPT-4 and it didn’t at GPT-3. Maybe it was much more human-like and it sort of crossed some perceptual chasm that made you think, “Oh my God, this thing is like a human.”But I’m not the only person who felt that. People at Microsoft also felt that — there was that whole “Sparks of AGI” paper that came out around that time. So that was sort of the banal explanation. But yeah, I’ve been talking to computers for a long time, like you have. I used to go on AOL Instant Messenger and talk to SmarterChild, which was absolutely not intelligent, but it was still fun to type something in and have a thing type back. So I grant that I am sort of obsessed with this technology.There’s a reason I’m asking this. I realize it’s funny that when reporting on AGI so much, I’m using alive in such a colloquial way, and it clearly means something else inside the AI industry. If you ask Anthropic if Claude is alive, they’re not like, “No,” but then they will start defining alive in very specific ways.[Laughs] They’ll say, “Its moral status is deeply uncertain.”So it’s alive. And they will get to, “Well, you have to have flesh and blood to be alive, obviously.” I will just set that aside. What I’m getting at is, I think if you went and talked to a GPT-4 class model today, you would not have the same experience. And maybe that’s just because you have the experience, but a lot of people have had that experience now.I think if you put a GPT-4 class model in front of your average Google AI Overviews user, they would not be confused about what was happening anymore. They would not say this is a step towards AGI. It’s that reframing — as the models get more and more capable, our expectations of them go up, but they also get higher.I’m asking about this in the context of AGI because “this thing can go off and find a bunch of PHP vulnerabilities” is one kind of intelligence, but “this thing can compete with another human being to have an emotional relationship with you,” or be your butler or whatever it is, feels like a different set of capabilities. That one to me feels flat.Well, I think that’s just saturated. How much more like a human could it communicate? There just isn’t a lot of room to run on that particular skill. Where I think they still have room to run is on solving novel problems in math and science and other things. But I believe that it talks like a human. It talks more like a human than many humans I know. So I think they kind of check the box on that one.“It talks more like a human than many humans I know” is absolutely a sign of you living in Silicon Valley talking to AI researchers all day long.Well, now everyone just talks like Claude. I’ve stopped counting the number of times I’m at a party and talking to someone, and they’re like, “Now that is a load-bearing fact.” Or they’ll say, “I hope that’s landing cleanly with you.”That’s really bad. Tell me about that. That’s a real back-and-forth. I’ve always joked with you and Casey that we should just start a show called “New York vs. California,” where I’m just openly skeptical of these claims and you guys are fully AGI-pilled. This is a culture. It’s a scene.The number of parties that show up in your book is astounding. There was a moment in reading your book where I was like, “I don’t think I’m going to enough parties.” All these people are always at parties and issuing proclamations to each other at parties. Tell me about that culture. Tell me about that scene.So it’s important to know that these are not always parties in the way that New Yorkers would think of parties. There are very few raves. There’s only one rave in the book. And Grimes was the DJ, and it was a kind of symbolic rave for the effective accelerationist movement.This is a great scene in the book because Grimes stops in the middle of her DJ set and says, “I don’t agree with any of you.”[Laughs] Then she keeps DJ-ing. Yeah, it’s incredible. But yes, there are a lot of parties. It’s a very small world. I mean, that’s part of the whole takeaway from the book. It’s not really a message book. I wasn’t trying to convince anyone of anything.But one thing that was apparent to me and that I think will be apparent to people who read the book is just that it is a super small subculture of people who have been making all the decisions. They all hang out, they all know each other. There are a bunch of people who are married to or dating people at different frontier AI companies. It’s just a small world.So yeah, there are parties. They have LAN parties. There’s a big group of AI researchers who play Age of Empires at a LAN party on the weekends. I just learned one of the labs has a poker game where they bring in people from other labs.So these people are all just kind of living and hanging out in San Francisco together, and I think that’s important to capture. Because you’re right, it is a whole scene. There’s a whole ethos. These people just hang out with each other all the time and this is how the norms are enforced and deepened.How do you think that collides with, “And we might also remake the world”? If you are in a small scene in San Francisco, and you’re all playing poker together and the conversation at the poker table is that we might be the last company, that is in conflict with, “Oh, there’s millions upon billions of other people in the world who might have a say.” And if I had to boil the backlash down, it’s that: “Oh, we should probably get a say here.”Totally. I think we should get a say here. I’m not saying that this is a good state of affairs where a couple hundred people in San Francisco are making all the decisions about how society goes.But as you were doing the reporting and the weight of the task and the consequences of the goal set in on these people, because that is the throughline of the book. The stakes just keep going up. At one point, Sergey Brin is like, “We’re going to get to AGI now,” and he just announces it at Google. It’s unclear whether Sundar Pichai thinks that is a good idea, but that is a thing that the cofounder of Google is announcing inside of Google.The stakes are just going up. The race to get there is just going up. But I just can’t get the image of it’s a bunch of people drinking beers, and being like, “Well, what if there was no money? What if physical scarcity was gone too and robots built all the houses?”This is like any party in San Francisco you go to. Someone will say some version of, “What’s your plan for the post-AGI future?” Or they’ll tell you how they’re really into the idea of whole brain emulation or mind uploading. There’s a lot of futurism happening out here. And look, again, I’m not saying this is good. In fact, maybe I should sell a version outside the Bay Area of the book that just has a “this is bad” appended to every factual claim.[Laughs] I don’t think it’s good or bad. Actually, I’m more neutral on that. I’m always wondering if the technology can accept the pressure. So my question about LLMs three years ago was, “Can it do all the things you want it to do?” Now it can definitely do some set of things that you want it to do. So now it’s, “Can these companies accept the weight of their own ambition?” I don’t know the answer to that question.I don’t either. And I think that we’re going to see a lot of growing pains. I mean, these are still very young companies. They still have a lot of growing to do.Do you think they’re going to make it? Actually, let’s do this as a lightning round. Do you think OpenAI will make it?Yes.Do you think Anthropic will make it?Yes.Do you think Google will make it?Yes.What does “make it” mean in your mind? They’re all going to be trillion-dollar, multi-AGI variant successes?Yes. I think, look, there will probably be those three, and then maybe one or two others that sort of make it. And make it for varying definitions of making it. There’ll be one or two big enterprise AI companies, one or two big consumer AI companies. But there just are network effects and winner-take-all dynamics or winner-take-most dynamics in these markets.There’s some people who believe in the mono-AGI, like the singleton theory, it’s often called, that there can only be one because once you have one AGI, it’s then going to go around melting the chips of the other AI labs, and they won’t be able to build theirs. But I think we’ll probably end up with a small handful of AGIs.What do you make of the idea that this is a pretty simple recipe, there are open-weight models, and there is a China, and that all the pricing power will be destroyed because a midrange open-weight model can do everything that you probably want it to do on a Mac?I don’t think so.No?Because you still have to pay for inference on those models. Even the open-weight models have to run on computers, and inference is getting more compute-intensive, not less, the more frontier these models get. So training budgets may fall, but inference budgets will be robust for the foreseeable future. You can run some tasks locally, but I think this is something that has been predicted since the first open-weight models that, “Oh, they were going to become commoditized and destroy demand.”But I think what we’re starting to learn is that there are a lot of people who will pay and want to pay for the absolute best model. They don’t want to be working with the slightly crappier model from six months ago. I also think once you crack down on distillation, which is this process whereby you can take a closed model and make a slightly dumber open version of it by just basically DDoSing the inference for the smarter model, it’s not clear to me that the quality of the open models will continue to be closely correlated with the quality of the closed models.The thing that really grabs me at that is they all did it to each other for a while, like Grok obviously distilled Claude, and it’s admitted to in the court documents. There is that class of second-tier companies. I would put in that category SpaceXSI, I believe it’s now technically known as.[Laughs] I haven’t checked my email in the last 30 minutes, so I don’t know what that company is called.It’s called SpaceXSITesla Inc. It’s all going to be one. Elon Inc. is what it’s called. They obviously distilled Claude to some huge extent. They’re now renting their compute to Anthropic. It’s unclear whether they will make the investment in having a leading model.Meta just announced its model, and they’re sort of back on the frontier, but they obviously care more about Muse than having a bleeding-edge model. There’s some dynamic there. Those companies don’t strike me as being run by idealistic true believers. Those are companies that need to invest in some technology to build some products. They just need to get there.Can you get there without the idealistic fervor?No, you can’t get there without the idealistic fervor. Well, let me clarify that, because I don’t think Sundar has the idealistic fervor, but Google might still get there.Because Sergey has the idealistic fervor.You need someone in a position of decision-making authority.You just need the cofounder of the company.Well, it might be enough for Meta to have Alexandr Wang, who, by all accounts, is a true believer. I don’t know that it literally has to be the CEO every time, but you need a dense nucleus of true believers to be able to convince you to lay out the money on GPUs.Or just you need someone who is like Mark Zuckerberg, one of the most competitive people in the world, who will just adopt whatever strategy he thinks will allow them to win. If that happens to align with building AGI, then maybe they’ll do it.Last question: I’ve asked you this several times, but are you AGI-pilled?Yes. Are you?No. I read your book, and it’s as close as I’ve ever gotten. That line about next-token prediction just always overcoming its skeptics just really hit me, because it has overcome my skepticism several times now.But this is why I was asking about talking to a chatbot from three years ago. I feel that wall in the kind of intelligence these things are. Even though I have set off agents to do all kinds of things, there’s a brittleness to it that feels inherent to the technology to me.Did the Millennium Prize solution change that view at all?Only in the sense that finding the next thing that has some objective verifiability seems very rich for these tools. So obviously mathematics has a verifiability, and the tools got so capable that they could run at it really, really hard. The brittleness that I’m describing is a lot of the world around us does not have that kind of verifiability.So I set off Muse to fill out a document on some janky government website, and the website cannot tell Muse what it’s getting right or wrong, and it just collapses. You can blame that on the underlying model not being at the frontier, but there’s just some part of that experience with LLM-based technologies that makes me feel they’re brittle in very specific ways, and they haven’t overcome that sensation for me.I’m not saying they’re not incredibly capable. I’m not saying that, as enterprise software, they will not automate virtually every business in the world in some way. I’m not saying that my wife isn’t a lawyer who uses Claude every day. It’s all there.But there’s some part of it where my skepticism is about whether it can overcome its brittleness to become the machine god. I’m excited to see if they can do it, but I don’t see the path from where I sit.You think there’s sort of a natural plateau at just below human-level intelligence?I think the human-level intelligence to me, and this is just more philosophical, is defined by novel problem solving — looking at a thing, and understanding that there are multiple paths to a solution, and not having one of those needing to be objectively right to get to the end.What would it take? What would you have to see to have the scales fall from your eyes and go, “I, Nilay Patel, am fully AGI-pilled”? What would convince you?I would have to see... You have young children. I have young children. There’s a thing that young children do where they fall down the stairs, and you just see the lights all go on: “I’ve learned this, I will know it forever, and now I’m going to build on that.”Maybe they’re going to announce recursive self-improvement at the AI labs and that will be the thing that drops the scales from my eyes. But the brittleness that I’m talking about is I see the opposite of that in my children. I’m assuming you see the opposite of it in yours. When they fail, they know about that failure forever. To me, there’s just something very, very core to being human, where every now and again I wake up, and I’m embarrassed about something that happened in high school, and that drives me to do a bunch of stuff, or it drives me to not make a bunch of decisions.I think that is just a key part of our intelligence. I’m not saying it has to be a key part of every intelligence, but the brittleness I see with the AI systems that I use today is that they’re still computers in a very specific way. They still act like computers. They’re good at solving problems that you can test. They’re good at software engineering. I don’t know that that way of thinking extends into every domain.I hope you’re right.That’s my point of view. I call it software brain. You hear the AI CEO say, “We solve coding, and now we can solve everything.” And to me, I’m saying, “That assumes everything happens inside of a computer, and in fact, most things don’t.”You sure? You sure your brain’s not just a fleshy computer?I am 100 percent sure of that.You’re not a computational functionalist?No. I think I’ve read this from you in the past, and I’ve certainly read it from other people, that the machines of our time dominate our own explanations of ourselves. So in the era of the steam engine, our self-conception was that we were steam engines, or in early computers, we were early computers, right? I still call it horsepowering through a problem because I’m a car person.You don’t think that the AI industry has convinced itself that they are AI because that is the machine of our time?I don’t know. I’m not a theory of mind guy. I’m not a cognitive neuroscientist. I think that to believe that what’s going on in your head and my head right now is not a form of computation, you have to be kind of a dualist or you have to be kind of a religious person. You have to think there is some spirit, some soul, some secret sauce of cognition that is not just data entering and being processed and transforming inputs into outputs.Look, I know that is the least romantic, most San Francisco way of explaining what human cognition is. I just have not heard a compelling argument that it is not how our brains work that doesn’t involve some sort of supernatural or immaterial substance.There’s a surprising number of neuroscientists and religious scholars listening to the show. They’re going to come find you.They will.I’m confident. Let me just ask you this. There’s a surprising amount of religiosity in Silicon Valley right now. We just published the Peter Thiel lectures on The Verge. He’s talking about the Antichrist. Do you think these ideas are connected, that we are building God such that they seek God?Yes. I think we will absolutely have AI religions. I think AI is posing all of the same questions as a religion that we would not otherwise be asking of God. “What is our purpose? What is our meaning? Why are we here?” These are the questions that people now talk about in the context of AI.I often tell people that being in San Francisco these days feels like living in Europe during the Reformation, where you just have crazy wild-eyed prophets waving their pamphlets around and trying to get you to join their thing. This is what walking down Market Street in San Francisco feels like.What dropped the scales from your eyes? What made you AGI-pilled?Bing’s Sydney, believe it or not.Yeah?I mean, that was the start. And then from there, it was just kind of a gradual process. One day I realized when I used these things, I wasn’t treating them like an intellectual inferior. I was in some ways treating them as a peer, and that’s when I realized, “Oh, something’s happened here.”So it’s possible I have AI psychosis. It would not be the first time I’ve heard that, but every time that I have thought, “Okay, it can’t possibly get any better than this, this has to be the plateau,” I’ve been wrong.So I’m just learning to approach these things with some humility, and maybe the crazy people who have been predicting that scaling would continue indefinitely are right. If they are, I think we need to learn about them, A, and why they think that, and B, try to figure out what to do about it.Well, Kevin, I’m confident the next time you come on the show, I will have set up a fully AI influencer to make money doing [user-generated content] ads, which is the true future of, I think, all of our businesses.The podcast is Machine Gods. It’s very good. You host it with Casey Newton. And the book is excellent. It’s The AGI Chronicles. Kevin, thank you so much for being on Decoder.Thanks. It was great to see you.Questions or comments? Hit us up at decoder@theverge.com. We really do read every email!Decoder with Nilay PatelA podcast from The Verge about big ideas and other problems.SUBSCRIBE NOW!
history.author: Nilay Patel
history.titleZh: 凯文·鲁斯成了AGI信徒。你为什么不是？
history.descriptionZh:
凯文·罗斯（Kevin Roose）是资深科技记者，曾长期供职于《纽约时报》并主持热门播客《Hard Fork》。近日，他与搭档凯西·牛顿（Casey Newton）离开《纽约时报》，创立了自己的科技播客《Machine Gods》，同时出版新书《The AGI Chronicles》（AGI编年史），详细记录了人工智能行业近年来的爆炸性变革以及各前沿实验室竞相构建通用人工智能（AGI）的历程。在本次访谈中，罗斯讨论了从传统媒体转向独立创作者的经历、新播客的定位，以及新书背后的深度报道过程。

**从传统媒体到独立创业**

罗斯表示，离开《纽约时报》创办独立公司是一个重大决定。他与牛顿共同创立播客公司，罗斯因掷硬币获胜而获得CEO头衔。他坦言，自己从未经营过企业，但逐渐发现商业运营的乐趣，尤其是对创始人角色的体验超出预期。他提到，媒体行业长期对全面投入YouTube等视频平台持谨慎态度，部分原因是结构性经济因素，部分是因为缺乏能够做出长期承诺的机构。但他认为，YouTube是当下全球最重要的媒体平台，而高质量新闻在其中的占比极小，因此他希望探索如何在YouTube上实现可持续的新闻视频模式。

《Machine Gods》与NPR合作，定位为“视频优先”的播客产品，将在YouTube、Apple Podcasts和Spotify等多平台分发。罗斯认为，YouTube是目前最稳定的媒体基础设施，难以被替代——要取代YouTube，不仅需要为创作者和用户提供更好的体验，还需要复制整个人类的视觉内容 corpus（例如数百万条水管工修理水槽的教学视频），这几乎不可能。

**AI报道受众的变化与“AI现实主义”**

罗斯观察到，AI报道的受众正在分化：一部分是构建AI产品的人，热衷消费所有相关内容；一部分是坚决反对AI的人，认为一切都是假的；而中间群体正在扩大——这些产品已变得更有用，人们开始以实际表现来评估它们。牛顿将此概括为“AI现实主义”：一大群人只是好奇、感兴趣，也许有些害怕，但他们的反应不是逃避，而是试图理解。

罗斯指出，过去一段时间市场上存在大量“安慰性”内容，告诉人们AI不会成真、不必关注。但多数人已经接受或对AI不会消失这一事实感到兴奋。他在《Hard Fork》时期就发现，即使是看似不符合节目调性的内容——比如Claude Code的实操教程——也能获得大量关注，说明人们确实想知道发生了什么。

**《The AGI Chronicles》：记录一场可能消失的历史**

罗斯写这本书的动机源于一种历史学者的紧迫感。他热爱阅读关于莱特兄弟、美国农村电气化、PC革命等重大创新时刻的书籍，注意到这些著作都依赖大量同时代的笔记和证据——科学家的实验记录、当事人之间的通信等。但在AI行业，这些材料正在系统性地消失：从业者受雇于私营企业，不受政府档案保存法规约束；Signal和Slack消息被律师设置为定期自动删除；研究人员忙于“研磨”模型，无暇记录。因此，他利用自己作为记者的“场边特权席位”，尽可能多地采访和记录（约150人），许多内容以背景方式呈现以保护受访者。

**AGI从梦想变为必须：转折点**

书中的一个核心主题是AGI从纯粹的梦想变为必须实现的目标。罗斯指出，AGI的概念由来已久，可以追溯到古代，艾伦·图灵就曾描述过能做出人脑所能做的一切的“思考机器”。但长期以来没有任何技术能够实现这一愿景——接收信息、学习关于信息的知识、并据此做出预测和行动。

关键的转折点是2017年谷歌开发并发表的Transformer架构。谷歌将其发表并展示给了包括OpenAI在内的多个机构，OpenAI抓住这一想法全力推进——这就是ChatGPT中的“T”。但具有讽刺意味的是，谷歌虽然发明了Transformer，却未能将其转化为产品，直到OpenAI率先做到。

罗斯认为，下一词预测（next-token prediction）至今尚未失败——它不断在每一个数量级上持续有效。他引用一种观点认为，人脑内部本质上也是大规模的下一词预测。这构成了AI的核心谜团：为什么下一词预测如此高效？他认为这可能是一个宇宙级的奥秘，但事实是下一词预测的泛化能力极强。

**各实验室的“AGI信仰”程度不一**

罗斯指出，各实验室对AGI的信念程度不同。Anthropic是最“AGI-pilled”（深信AGI）的实验室，OpenAI紧随其后。谷歌则一直难以“感受AGI”。书中记录了谷歌内部的一场备忘录论战：一位研究员撰写《Say AGI》，主张谷歌若想在AI领域获胜、招募顶尖人才并保持安全，就必须承认他们正在构建的不仅仅是让Gmail或Google Photos更好的工具，而是通向人类水平通用智能的东西。随即另一位员工撰写《Don't Say AGI》，称这是一个可怕的不科学术语。至今谷歌CEO桑达尔·皮查伊（Sundar Pichai）仍不说AGI，而德米斯·哈萨比斯（Demis Hassabis）和谢尔盖·布林（Sergey Brin）则说。罗斯认为谷歌内部存在派系：一方认为这仍是疯狂的想法，应将其作为窄工具来讨论；另一方则认为必须宣称自己在构建AGI，否则顶尖人才会流向OpenAI或Anthropic。

**商业压力与AGI信念的双刃剑**

罗斯认为，对AGI的信念是一把双刃剑。一方面，如果CEO极度“AGI-pilled”，就很难关心利润率、企业客户等琐事；另一方面，信念是AI成功的关键 ingredient——正是信念驱动了“押上农场”的决策，而这些决策确实获得了回报。他举例说，一年前所有人都在质疑OpenAI在计算上花费太多，而一年后OpenAI是唯一没有严重计算约束的主要AI公司。正是萨姆·奥尔特曼（Sam Altman）及其高管去年对计算的大举押注，使OpenAI今天处于比谷歌、Anthropic、Meta更有利的位置。

关于OpenAI的“blip”（奥尔特曼被解雇又回归的事件），罗斯认为这标志着OpenAI从研究公司转变为商业公司。但他强调，OpenAI砍掉Sora等副业、聚焦编程和长周期代理工作负载，本质上仍是AGI押注——因为真正通向AGI的路径是通过构建优秀的编程模型并让其自我递归改进，这是目前领先的AGI路径。

**理想主义者能否管理万亿美元公司？**

罗斯指出，这些创始人都是理想主义者，以至于彼此分道扬镳创办各自的公司。但没有人有过从零收入到五年内可能实现2万亿美元IPO的经验——这从未发生过。他认为他们正在“一边建造飞机一边冲向事件视界”，但做得已经尽可能好。他不认为引入可口可乐式的职业CEO是个好主意，因为这些人是狂热者和传教士。他提到，一位前沿公司的人曾告诉他，他们公司可能是“最后一家公司”——“资本主义的目的论终点，可能再也不会有另一家主要由人类运营的大公司。”

**为何不停止？三种理由**

罗斯采访了约150人，询问“如果这么危险，为什么还要做？”答案大致分三类：第一是减少伤害的论点——“总有人会构建这个，配方并不难，只需要大量计算、数据和正确的算法。如果可能，它就会发生，由我们来而不是我们不信任的人来做更好。”第二是真正的信徒——“只要我们能安全地渡过难关，一切都会变得很好。”第三是纯粹觉得有趣——“这很好玩，我喜欢让神经网络写代码。”

**对“AI反弹”的看法**

罗斯认为AI公司并不对反弹感到意外，也不喜欢反弹。一位CEO曾对他说：“我理解，我们还没有治愈任何疾病。我们确实认为工具能做有趣的事，但在重大社会改善方面还没有太多成绩。”一些人遗憾聊天机器人先于癌症治愈出现，但技术树就是这样生长的。现在唯一负责任的做法是继续推进癌症治愈，以便当人们审视AI对生活的影响时，能看到“我的祖母还活着，如果没有AI发现的药物她就不会在这里”。

**谷歌的困境与DeepMind的威胁**

罗斯回顾了谷歌对AI的态度：任务型软件——让搜索好10%、Gmail好5%，持续部署改进，凭借数据访问和规模优势保持领先。但OpenAI出现并进入Bing，引发了市场震动。谷歌被迫反应，但并未全力投入。书中引用马斯克诉奥尔特曼案的庭审记录显示，OpenAI创始人都对谷歌、特别是哈萨比斯感到恐惧。罗斯认为这种恐惧是合理的：2015至2016年，DeepMind是唯一真正重要的AGI实验室，在围棋、星际争霸等游戏中获胜，深度强化学习似乎可能一路扩展到AGI。如果AlphaGo Zero能在几小时内从零到击败世界最佳棋手，那么也许可以将围棋替换为数学或编程，快速攀登任务阶梯。虽然事实证明没有LLM不行，但在另一个平行宇宙中，DeepMind可能最先到达AGI。

**技术路径：LLM是否足够？**

罗斯表示，对LLM持怀疑态度的人常回归“世界模型”理念——认为要实现AGI必须能视觉理解物理世界、驱动机器人。但他本人相信“一切都是软件”，LLM是最有希望的路径。也许需要对架构做些调整、构建持续学习方法，但所有实验室都在押注LLM将继续有效。

**关于Bing Sydney与“活着”的讨论**

牛顿提到2023年Bing的Sydney聊天机器人事件，当时罗斯的《纽约时报》文章标题为“Bing's AI chat: 'I want to be alive'”，引发广泛关注。罗斯澄清他从未说Sydney是活的，文章中明确表示他不认为Sydney有感知。但他承认，现在对当今AI系统的“意识概率”评估比2023年的模型更高。他认为Sydney之所以令人毛骨悚然，一个平庸的解释是：那是GPT-4的首次公开部署——微软在未完全准备好的情况下将其塞进了Bing。GPT-4相比GPT-3在对话体验上有主观上的阶跃变化，可能跨越了某种感知鸿沟，让人们觉得“这东西像人”。微软同期发表的“Sparks of AGI”论文也反映了同样的感受。

**关于“活着”的语义与能力饱和**

牛顿指出，随着模型能力提升，人们对它们的期望也在提高。罗斯认为，在“像人一样交流”这一维度上已经饱和——没有太多提升空间。但在解决数学和科学中的新问题等方面仍有大量空间。他提到，现在硅谷的人说话都像Claude——“这是一个承重事实”“我希望这能清晰地传达给你”等表达已成为日常。

**AI社交场景与“最后一家公司”文化**

罗斯描述了AI行业的社交场景：这是一个非常小的亚文化群体，彼此相识，许多人跨实验室约会或结婚。有LAN派对玩《帝国时代》，有跨实验室的扑克局。书中记录了一场Grimes担任DJ的加速主义运动派对，她在演出中途说“我不同意你们任何人”然后继续打碟。罗斯认为，这个小型社交圈与“我们可能重塑世界”之间的冲突，正是反弹的核心——“哦，我们大概应该在这里有发言权。”

**这些公司能否“成功”？**

在闪电问答中，罗斯预测OpenAI、Anthropic和谷歌都会“成功”——成为万亿美元级别的公司，可能还有一两家其他公司。他认为存在网络效应和赢家通吃或赢家通吃大部分的动态。虽然有人相信“单例理论”（一旦有一个AGI，它会去融化其他实验室的芯片），但他认为最终会有少数几个AGI。

关于开源模型和中国竞争是否会摧毁定价权，罗斯不认同。他指出推理成本仍在上升而非下降，即使开源模型也需要在计算机上运行，推理越来越计算密集。训练预算可能下降，但推理预算在可预见的未来将保持强劲。人们愿意为绝对最好的模型付费，不想用六个月前稍差的模型。此外，一旦打击蒸馏（通过大量调用更聪明模型的推理来制造稍笨的开源版本），开源模型的质量与闭源模型质量之间的紧密关联可能不再成立。

**需要理想主义狂热**

罗斯认为，没有理想主义的狂热就无法到达AGI。虽然皮查伊可能没有这种狂热，但谷歌有布林。或者Meta有亚历山大·王（Alexandr Wang），一位公认的真正信徒。你需要在决策权威位置上有真正信徒，或者像马克·扎克伯格这样极具竞争力的人，采用任何他认为能赢的策略。

**罗斯的AGI信念与牛顿的怀疑**

罗斯承认自己是“AGI-pilled”。他的转折点正是Bing Sydney——从那开始，逐渐意识到自己不再把这些工具当作智力上的劣等者，而是在某些方面当作同行。每当他以为“这肯定是平台期了”，他都错了。他正在学习以谦逊的态度对待这些事物，也许那些预测缩放将持续无限的“疯狂的人”是对的。

牛顿则表示自己不是AGI-pilled，尽管罗斯的书让他比以往任何时候都更接近。他认为这些系统存在一种固有的脆弱性。他举例说，让Muse去填写某个简陋政府网站上的文件，网站无法告诉Muse对错，它就崩溃了。他认为数学等具有客观可验证性的领域非常适合这些工具，但世界的大部分并不具备这种可验证性。他怀疑LLM能否克服脆弱性成为“机器神”。

罗斯回应说，要相信人脑中的活动不是一种计算形式，就必须是二元论者或宗教信徒，必须认为存在某种精神、灵魂或认知的秘密配方，不仅仅是数据输入、处理和转换。他承认这是“最不浪漫、最旧金山的解释方式”，但他没有听到过不涉及超自然或非物质实体的有力反驳。

**AI与宗教**

罗斯认为AI将与宗教产生深刻关联。AI提出了与宗教相同的问题：“我们的目的是什么？我们的意义是什么？我们为什么在这里？”他说，现在在旧金山的感觉就像生活在宗教改革时期的欧洲，到处是眼睛发亮的先知挥舞着小册子试图让你加入他们的事业。他相信绝对会出现AI宗教。

**结语**

牛顿表示，下次罗斯来节目时，他可能已经设立了一个全AI网红来做UGC广告赚钱——这才是所有人业务的真正未来。《Machine Gods》播客与凯西·牛顿共同主持，已上线。《The AGI Chronicles》一书已出版。

history.title: Cadence reveals Maestro, fine-tuned AI models built to run specialized chip design agents, with early access coming for 'select customers' in Q4 2026
history.description: Cadence unveiled Maestro, domain-specialized AI models for its chip design agents, with early access for select customers in Q4 2026.
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Cadence, one of the largest electronic design automation (EDA) companies, has unveiled Maestro, its new portfolio of domain-specialized AI models tailored for its chip design agents, in a press release sent just ahead of earnings. In initial results compared with general-purpose AI models, Cadence claims up to a 30% improvement in the quality of results and that Maestro effectively uses fewer tokens for the same task, with up to 5x the token efficiency. The first models “are available to select early access customers” in Q4 2026, and customers may run them on Cadence’s cloud, public clouds, or customer-controlled on-premises environments and post-train them on their own “proprietary data, designs, and workflows.” To learn more about Maestro, we spoke with two Cadence executives: Rob Knoth, senior group director of strategy and new ventures, and Paul Cunningham, senior vice president and general manager.This approach is distinct from Synopsys’ own specialized model, GPT-Synopsys, which will run on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure, without using customer data to train the model. The models of both EDA giants, announced less than a month apart, now split on where a customer’s design data goes. Where they might not differ is why: Paul Cunningham, senior vice president and general manager at Cadence, told Tom’s Hardware Premium that agent costs have “really started to explode,” adding, “And I think the world realized so.” That makes it a natural step, he said, to move more of the agents’ iterating “into the weights of the models themselves.” (Image credit: Cadence)Maestro takes this step through Cadence’s AI Super Agents, which “interpret design intent, decompose tasks” and “orchestrate the Maestro portfolio with other leading frontier and open-weight models,” evaluating trade-offs to guide decisions with domain expertise. It also uses reinforcement learning (RL), where Cadence’s “deterministic solvers evaluate outputs against engineering objectives, constraints and ground truth,” and, importantly, the results feed back into the models for improvement.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The models include Nvidia’s Nemotron, and customers can run the customer-data training step themselves with Cadence’s fine-tuning harness, potentially “on their own GPUs, on their own network,” Cunningham said. He added that Nemotron, specifically, was “giving really solid results and actually improving very, very fast.”One constant that keeps popping up with agentic EDA is the need to nail down what the numbers actually measure. In chip design, quality of results usually refers to the design’s power, performance, and area, though Cadence didn’t specify what its 30% figure measures. Both it and the 5x token efficiency figure are measured against “a general-purpose foundation model,” which Cadence told us is the open-source model Maestro started from before its training. The company wouldn’t name the foundational AI model that Maestro is derived from beyond mentioning that it is “one of the leading open source models that’s very competitive with commercial frontier models.” You may like The state of agentic AI in chip design tools in 2026 Synopsys debuts Autopilot platform for developing chips autonomously using AI OpenAI and Synopsys partner to build "GPT-Synopsys" for autonomous chip design Cadence credits the token savings to balancing its EDA and system design automation (SDA) “tool calls with LLM invocations.” As an analogy, Cunningham said, “You don’t need to drive to Safeway in the jet engine,” and you want to use “the right model at the right time for the right task.”Runtime does matter, too: as Rob Knoth, senior group director of strategy and new ventures at Cadence, told Tom’s Hardware Premium in September that a tool call could take anywhere from hours to days to return a value, while the AI industry’s training loops are “used to minutes.” Efficiency could also lower costs, since Maestro use counts toward Cadence’s agent pricing, a subscription with a consumption allowance and charges for use beyond it, Cunningham said. He didn’t say whether the token savings cut a customer’s bill.Being flexible for the customer is a key element of any solution, and for Cadence’s competitor Synopsys, this lies in Autopilot, which Synopsys says allows customers to “choose among commercial, open-source, and fine-tuned language models” across “Synopsys-managed and customer-managed deployments,” with cloud or on-premises infrastructure. For agent security, such as sandboxing, Cadence says it’s working with Nvidia on an integration with Nvidia’s OpenShell Reference Architecture, which Nvidia launched last week, naming both Cadence and Synopsys. These options can help protect customer intellectual property. Swipe to scroll horizontally Cadence Maestro vs. GPT-Synopsys Header Cell - Column 0 Cadence Maestro GPT-Synopsys Announced Oct. 26, 2026 Sept. 30, 2026 What it is A portfolio of domain-specialized AI models for Cadence’s AI Super Agents A specialized model that operates Synopsys’ tools directly Model partner Nvidia (Nemotron, OpenShell) OpenAI Models Post-trained LLMs, trained decision models and agent skills, blended with frontier and open-weight models, including Nemotron OpenAI frontier models Where it runs Cadence’s cloud, public clouds or customer-controlled on-premises environments OpenAI-hosted infrastructure Customer data Customers can post-train it on their own data, designs and workflows, with Cadence’s fine-tuning tools Customer data isn’t used to train the model Claimed results Up to 30% higher quality of results and up to 5x token efficiency vs. a general-purpose foundation model, the unnamed open-source model Maestro started from (initial results; measure not stated) None disclosed Availability First models to select early-access customers in Q4 2026 No date; early technology engagements underway Customers named Socionext, Silicon Labs (Nvidia as partner), frontier AI labs None Pricing Subscription with a usage allowance, then charged by use Not disclosed; Synopsys and OpenAI share revenue under their deal Cadence has had a busy 12 months with customers and agents alike. During Cadence’s July earnings call, CEO Anirudh Devgan said ChipStack, its design and verification agent, “has more than 20 customer engagements,” and ViraStack, its custom and analog agent, “more than 25 customer engagements.” Socionext said just last week that it was applying InnoStack. Silicon Labs has also credited ChipStack with accelerating debugging, and both companies say they are watching Maestro next.Cadence's agentic consolidation began with its acquisition of ChipStack back in November 2025. In June 2026, the company claimed that its agent had reached Level 5 autonomy, which we explored in detail. In September, Knoth teased Maestro’s ingredients to Tom's Hardware Premium a month early, two days before the GPT-Synopsys announcement: “reinforcement learning loops, domain-specific post-training of open-weight models, model routing.” Maestro is now sitting under all four super agents, targeting a similar year-end window to Synopsys’ Autopilot; the table below has the full timeline. Swipe to scroll horizontally Cadence’s agentic AI roadmap When Product Cadence’s claim Status and what’s due November 2025 ChipStack acquisition (agentic verification startup) — Done; co-founder Kartik Hegde now leads Cadence’s core AI research group February 2026 ChipStack AI Super Agent Up to 10x productivity for coding designs and testbenches, test plans, regressions and debug In early access since launch April 2026 ViraStack (custom and analog), InnoStack (digital implementation) and AgentStack (head agent) — Socionext is deploying InnoStack in production; others not stated June 2026 ChipStack at Level 5, with Nvidia’s Nemotron and OpenShell Over 40x faster RTL validation cycles in Nvidia’s deployment Level 5 and AgentStack due to early-access customers in the second half of 2026 July 2026 AuraStack (PCB and advanced packaging) Up to 2x faster time to market and 15x higher productivity Available on Cadence’s Millennium M2000 supercomputer; Nokia is deploying it (Oct. 21) September 2026 ChipStack RTL Generation Agent An average of 24% less area and 18% less power than pure foundation-model code, in early evaluations Due to select early-access customers in Q4 2026; early collaboration with Honda R&D Oct. 26, 2026 Maestro AI Model Portfolio Up to 30% higher quality of results and up to 5x token efficiency vs. a general-purpose foundation model, in initial results First models available to select early-access customers in Q4 2026; about a dozen engagements This rapid pace of progress means that a clear distinction has to be made between early access and general availability. Both Cadence and Synopsys can point to customer engagements, and, at least in the latter’s case for the AgentEngineer portfolio and Autopilot platform, general availability remains a goal by year’s end; Cadence hasn’t given a general availability date for Maestro. For GPT-Synopsys, though, only “early technology engagements are underway,” according to its partners. The platforms and agents remain works in progress.For Maestro, Cunningham hopes for “more case studies, more quantifiable benefits” through Q4. The real story, as he aptly put it, is that “we’re going to bring agents and agentic AI natively into our vertical, not that our vertical is going to get embedded into general-purpose agents.” Only customer results on real workflows will test Cadence’s 30% number, but going by what both companies have shown so far, their own early figures are extremely promising and exciting for the EDA industry.
history.author: Shane Downing
history.titleZh: Cadence发布Maestro：专为运行专用芯片设计智能体而打造的微调AI模型，将于2026年第四季度向“精选客户”开放早期访问
history.descriptionZh:
Cadence近日发布Maestro——一套面向芯片设计智能体的领域专用AI模型组合。该产品在财报前公布，被视为Cadence在“智能体化EDA”竞争中的关键布局。此前不到一个月，Synopsys刚发布GPT-Synopsys，两大EDA厂商几乎同时把生成式AI从通用模型推进到芯片设计专用模型。Cadence高管表示，智能体调用成本“已开始爆炸式增长”，因此有必要把智能体的大量迭代“移入模型权重本身”，让领域模型承担更多推理和决策工作。

技术层面，Maestro通过Cadence的AI Super Agents工作：智能体负责理解设计意图、分解任务，并将Maestro模型组合与其他前沿模型、开放权重模型协同调度，结合领域知识评估权衡并指导决策。Maestro采用强化学习，由Cadence的确定性求解器依据工程目标、约束和 ground truth 评估输出，再将结果反馈给模型以持续改进。模型组合包括Nvidia Nemotron，客户可使用Cadence的微调工具链，在自有GPU和网络上用自己的专有数据、设计和流程对模型进行后训练。部署方式包括Cadence云、公有云以及客户自控的本地环境。

性能方面，Cadence称在初步结果中，Maestro相较通用基础模型可实现最高30%的“结果质量”提升，并在同一任务中最多提升5倍token效率，即用更少token完成相同工作。不过，Cadence未说明30%具体衡量的是哪项指标；在芯片设计中，QoR通常指功耗、性能和面积。5倍token效率的对比基线是Maestro训练前所基于的某个未具名开源通用基础模型。Cadence将token节省归因于在EDA和系统设计自动化工具调用与大模型调用之间做平衡，以及“在正确时间用正确模型做正确任务”的模型路由思路。公司还指出，工具调用可能需要数小时到数天返回结果，而AI训练循环通常以分钟计，因此效率提升也可能影响成本；Maestro使用会计入Cadence智能体订阅的用量额度，超额部分另行计费，但Cadence未明确token节省是否会直接降低客户账单。首批模型将于2026年第四季度向部分早期访问客户提供，约有十余项合作，已提及Socionext、Silicon Labs以及前沿AI实验室等客户或合作伙伴。

与Synopsys的GPT-Synopsys相比，两者最大差异在于客户设计数据的流向。GPT-Synopsys于2026年9月30日发布，运行在OpenAI托管基础设施上，使用OpenAI前沿模型直接操作Synopsys工具，客户数据不用于训练该模型；目前仅处于早期技术合作阶段，未披露性能数据、可用日期和客户。Maestro则由Nvidia Nemotron和OpenShell等组成模型与安全基础，允许客户用自有数据后训练，并可在Cadence云、公有云或客户本地环境运行，强调客户对数据和部署的控制。Synopsys的Autopilot平台则允许客户在商业模型、开源模型和微调模型之间选择，并支持Synopsys管理或客户管理、云端或本地部署。安全方面，Cadence正与Nvidia合作集成OpenShell参考架构，以支持沙箱等智能体安全能力，保护客户知识产权。定价上，Maestro采用带用量额度的订阅制，超额按使用计费；GPT-Synopsys未披露定价，Synopsys与OpenAI按协议分享收入。

Maestro也处在Cadence快速扩张的智能体路线图之下。Cadence于2025年11月收购智能体验证初创公司ChipStack，随后推出ChipStack、ViraStack、InnoStack、AgentStack、AuraStack等智能体，覆盖设计验证、定制与模拟、数字实现、PCB与先进封装等环节。Cadence称ChipStack已有20多项客户合作，ViraStack有25多项；Socionext正在生产环境部署InnoStack，Silicon Labs称ChipStack加速了调试，Nokia则部署AuraStack。2026年6月，Cadence称ChipStack达到Level 5自主性，并在Nvidia部署中实现RTL验证周期超过40倍加速；9月发布的ChipStack RTL生成智能体在早期评估中相较纯基础模型生成代码平均减少24%面积、18%功耗，并与本田研发有早期合作。Maestro目前位于Cadence多类AI Super Agents之下，目标时间窗口与Synopsys的Autopilot相近。

整体来看，Maestro代表了EDA智能体从“调用通用大模型”向“领域专用模型+强化学习+模型路由+客户自有数据后训练”的演进。其潜在影响包括降低token消耗和智能体运行成本、提升芯片设计QoR、支持本地化和专有数据保护，并覆盖RTL生成、验证、模拟/定制设计、数字实现和先进封装等场景。但Cadence尚未给出Maestro的正式通用可用日期，30%提升的具体指标也未披露；Synopsys的Autopilot则将通用可用作为年底目标，GPT-Synopsys仍处早期阶段。Cadence高管希望第四季度获得更多案例和可量化收益，并强调真正的故事是“把智能体和智能体AI原生地带入EDA垂直领域，而不是把EDA嵌入通用智能体”。最终，30%的性能主张仍需真实客户工作流验证，但两家公司目前披露的早期数据已显示出对EDA行业的重要潜力。

history.title: Intel's Lip-Bu Tan has spoken with Lisa Su about potential collaboration with AMD
history.description: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan has reportedly discussed potential areas of cooperation with AMD chief Lisa Su as Intel works to rebuild its CPU business and expand its foundry operations. The companies have already collaborated on x86 standards and CPU software, including AMD’s integration of its ZenDNN optimizations into Intel’s oneDNN library. Neither executive has publicly detailed the reported discussions or confirmed a new agreement.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Intel and AMD have spent decades competing for the processors inside PCs and data centers, but the rivalry hasn't stopped the two companies from working together when their interests align. And now, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan has reportedly discussed potential areas of cooperation with AMD chief Lisa Su, adding another possible partnership to the mix as Intel tries to regain its footing in the semiconductor industry.According to a recording (embedded below) of Tan’s October 24 fireside chat with Chinese American Semiconductor Professional Association (CASPA) President Jimmy Cheng, the Intel CEO outlined his plans to rebuild the company’s CPU business, develop chips tailored to specific customer workloads, and attract more customers to its foundry operations. However, Tan did not publicly detail the reported areas of potential cooperation with AMD CEO Lisa Su.Intel has traditionally built its business around its own processor roadmaps, but Tan says the company needs to be more flexible as customers look for silicon designed for particular workloads. He pointed to Intel's Xeon processors as one area where that approach is changing, alongside continued development of GPUs and accelerators.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: "We have to reclaim the leadership in CPU. That is something that I am very determined to do." Tan said. Fireside Chat of Lip-Bu Tan and Jimmy Cheng - YouTube Watch On He also described a change in how Intel approaches customization. "Intel is so proud they never want to modify for customer needs," he said. "I'm modifying it for customer needs, and so that, I think, to me, is a fast-growing area, and I'm double, triple down on it." You may like AMD and Intel will work together to create a single PyTorch code path for AI inference on CPUs Intel licenses Atom-class x86 cores to startup AMD seeks 'broader partnership' with Samsung as it looks to secure memory supply The strategy extends beyond conventional CPUs, with Tan identifying application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), co-packaged optics (CPO), physical AI, and advanced packaging as potential growth businesses. He wants two or three of these areas to eventually contribute around 10% of Intel's revenue each.Intel's foundry business is another major part of Tan's plans. He said the company's 18A manufacturing process had reached volume production, while development of its next-generation 14A process was progressing strongly. Intel has already released version 0.5 of the 14A process design kit (PDK), which provides chip designers with the technical information and tools needed to develop products for the process.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsTan said version 0.9 was coming next, followed by version 1.0 for volume production in early 2027. "We have multiple customers [who] really want us to really scale their business," he said, referring to interest in Intel's foundry services.However, Intel did not identify those customers or disclose the size of any potential manufacturing orders during the discussion. Notably, in January, Intel had two prospective customers evaluating 14A test chips, with firm supplier decisions expected during the second half of 2026 and the first half of 2027. Tan also described foundry manufacturing as a business where trust matters as much as technology. Customers hand over wafers that will eventually become products on which their own revenue depends, making missed deadlines or manufacturing problems costly. "The moment we take on the foundry, take on the wafer is a lot of responsibility to make them successful," he said.He recalled one customer who had waited six to eight months hoping he would become CEO before presenting 15 areas where Intel had fallen short. Tan said he addressed the problems individually, after which the customer agreed to deepen its relationship with Intel.That said, the prospect of further cooperation would not be entirely new. In October 2024, Intel and AMD established the x86 Ecosystem Advisory Group alongside other technology companies to coordinate improvements to the x86 instruction set architecture and make it easier for hardware and software developers to support both companies' processors.That cooperation has since moved into AI software. Last week, it emerged that AMD was integrating its ZenDNN optimizations into Intel's open-source oneDNN library, bringing the companies' CPU optimization work for PyTorch AI inference under a common software path. The companies have also worked together on Advanced Matrix Extensions and other x86 capabilities through the advisory group, showing that they cooperate on shared technologies while continuing to compete for customers. For now, however, neither company has announced a new agreement arising from the discussions.
history.author: Newton Gitonga
history.titleZh: 英特尔陈立武已与苏姿丰讨论与AMD的潜在合作
history.descriptionZh:
英特尔与AMD长期以来在PC和数据中心处理器市场激烈竞争，但在共同利益驱动下也曾多次合作。最新报道显示，英特尔CEO陈立武（Lip-Bu Tan）已与AMD CEO苏姿丰（Lisa Su）讨论了潜在合作领域，为两家公司的关系再添一种可能的合作方向。相关消息源自陈立武10月24日与美籍华人半导体专业人士协会（CASPA）主席Jimmy Cheng炉边谈话的录音。陈立武在谈话中介绍了重振英特尔CPU业务、开发针对特定客户工作负载的定制芯片、吸引更多客户使用其代工服务的计划，但并未公开披露与苏姿丰讨论的具体合作领域。

在CPU业务方面，陈立武明确表示要重新夺回英特尔在CPU领域的领导地位。他指出，英特尔过去习惯于按照自身处理器路线图推进业务，但客户越来越需要针对特定工作负载设计的芯片，因此公司必须更加灵活。他以至强（Xeon）处理器为例说明这一转变，同时英特尔仍将继续开发GPU和加速器。陈立武还特别谈到定制化思路的变化：过去英特尔“非常骄傲，不愿为客户需求修改产品”，而现在他正推动根据客户需求进行修改，并将这一方向视为快速增长领域，表示会“加倍、三倍投入”。

这一战略不仅限于传统CPU。陈立武将专用集成电路（ASIC）、共封装光学（CPO）、物理AI和先进封装列为潜在增长业务，希望其中两到三个领域最终各自贡献约10%的英特尔营收。CPO通过将光引擎与芯片封装更紧密集成，有望提升互连带宽和能效；ASIC则面向特定客户工作负载提供定制化算力；先进封装则是提升芯片性能和集成度的重要环节。这些布局反映出英特尔试图从单一处理器供应商向更广泛的定制化计算和制造平台转型。

代工业务是陈立武计划的另一重点。他表示，英特尔18A制程已进入量产阶段，下一代14A制程开发进展强劲。英特尔已发布14A工艺设计套件（PDK）0.5版本，为芯片设计人员提供开发该制程产品所需的技术信息和工具；0.9版本即将推出，面向量产的1.0版本计划于2027年初发布。陈立武称，有多个客户希望英特尔帮助其扩大业务规模，但英特尔未透露客户身份或潜在订单规模。今年1月，曾有报道称两家潜在客户在评估14A测试芯片，最终供应商决策预计在2026年下半年和2027年上半年作出。陈立武还强调，代工制造不仅是技术问题，更是信任问题：客户交来的晶圆最终将变成其收入所依赖的产品，错过期限或制造问题都会带来高昂代价。他回忆，一位客户曾等待六到八个月、希望他成为CEO后才提出英特尔存在的15个不足；在逐一解决这些问题后，该客户同意深化与英特尔的关系。

值得注意的是，英特尔与AMD的进一步合作并非完全没有基础。2024年10月，两家公司已联合其他科技企业成立x86生态系统咨询小组，旨在协调x86指令集架构改进，降低硬件和软件开发者为两家处理器提供支持的难度。这一合作已延伸到AI软件领域：上周有消息称，AMD正将其ZenDNN优化集成到英特尔开源oneDNN库中，使两家公司面向PyTorch AI推理的CPU优化工作纳入共同软件路径。ZenDNN是AMD的CPU深度学习推理加速库，oneDNN是英特尔开源深度学习库，二者整合有助于开发者在AMD和英特尔CPU上获得更统一的AI推理优化支持。两家公司还通过该咨询小组在高级矩阵扩展（AMX）等x86能力上开展合作，说明它们可以在共享技术标准上合作，同时在客户市场继续竞争。不过，目前两家公司均未宣布由上述讨论产生的新协议。

总体来看，这一消息的核心意义在于：面对AI计算需求多样化、定制芯片兴起以及x86生态面临的竞争压力，英特尔正试图以更灵活的定制化策略、先进制程代工和开放软件合作重塑自身定位；而与AMD在x86生态和AI软件优化上的潜在或既有合作，可能降低开发者的适配成本、增强x86架构整体竞争力，但具体合作范围和商业影响仍有待官方确认。

history.title: Nvidia RTX 20, 30, and 40-series GPUs hacked to remove a half-speed AI throttle
history.description: Linux kernel modules lift Nvidia’s half-rate AI tensor limit on GeForce RTX 20, 30, and 40-series GPUs.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Modders have discovered a way to remove imposed half-speed AI performance limits on Nvidia RTX 20, 30, and 40-series GPUs with a firmware exploit, VideoCardz reports. Without the limitation, the RTX 4090 can achieve double its peak tensor rate, and matrix math can improve by up to 80% for the RTX 3090 Ti, with gains on other cards varying. Real workloads gain significantly less than the RTX 4090’s doubled peak would imply, and chatbot token speeds remain about the same, as that performance is dependent on memory bandwidth.For all impacted GeForce generations, Nvidia imposed a limit that, per its own published specs, runs FP32-accumulate math at half each card’s FP16-accumulate rate. That does not apply to its Turing and Ampere pro cards. The unlock returns native matrix-math throughput to owners of the cards, which can speed up prompt processing and image generation.Three separate projects offer generation unlocks, each with its own unofficial Linux module, while experimental Windows builds pursue a different approach. Card coverage varies by generation, with gpu-unlock handling Ampere and listing the GA102/GA103/GA104/GA106 series IDs. An Ada fork, gpu-unlock-ada, covers the RTX 4090 and, experimentally, the 4090 D, 4070 Ti Super, and the 4060 Ti 16GB. The turing-unlock project, adapted from gpu-unlock, works with the RTX 2080 Ti. See Table 1 for a breakdown.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Swipe to scroll horizontally Which GeForce cards each unlock covers Generation Project Cards with reported results Experimental or untested RTX 20 (Turing) turing-unlock RTX 2080 Ti (22GB memory-modded cards) Other Turing GPUs, added untested; FP16 only, since Turing lacks BF16 support RTX 30 (Ampere) gpu-unlock RTX 3090 Ti, 3090, 3080 10GB, 3080 20GB (memory-modded), 3070, 3060 12GB RTX 3070 Ti and GA103 cards untested; one RTX 3080 Ti 20GB OEM card stays at half rate RTX 40 (Ada Lovelace) gpu-unlock-ada RTX 4090 RTX 4090 D, 4070 Ti Super, 4060 Ti 16GB (experimental, one card each) RTX 50 (Blackwell) None — Not supported; gpu-unlock’s developer calls it out of scope How much faster the cards getThe peak doubling is for tensor rates, with the Ada fork developer’s RTX 4090 moving from 165.6 to 331.6 TFLOPS on FP16 and 165.5 to 330.6 TFLOPS on BF16. The gpu-unlock-ada README states that, in one independent owner’s matrix-multiply benchmark, cuBLAS GEMM medians only saw improvements of 12–34% and up to 20%, respectively. A separate data point, for an RTX 4070 Ti on Windows, saw larger matrix-multiply gains of +80.1% and +76.4%, the difference possibly caused by power limits.In the matrix-multiply benchmark, a tested RTX 3090 Ti scored +35% for FP16, +80% for BF16, and +94% for TF32, based on a user’s test with a modified Nvidia driver. The gpu-unlock README lists BF16 matrix-multiply gains from user reports of +25–67% for the RTX 3090, +70–73% for the 3080 10GB, +56–59% for a memory-modded 20GB version, +73–81% for the 3070, and around +80% for the 3060 12GB, though it notes they are not directly comparable. The power limit “matters a lot”: the lowest figure, +25%, came from cards capped at 225 W. For Ampere, LLM prefill improved 14–36%, with diffusion and FlashAttention speeding up, but LLM decode and INT8 stayed “about the same.” You may like Nvidia app update fails to block unofficial DLSS multi-frame generation mod on RTX 40 series gaming GPUs We tested DLSS Multi Frame Generation on RTX 40-series GPUs All-in-one 'DLSS Unlocked' mod brings DLSS 5 and multi-frame gen to RTX 20, 30, and 40 series An RTX 2080 Ti with a 22GB memory mod, a Dell OEM card limited to 250 W, saw FP16 matrix-multiply improvements of +36% to +64% depending on size; BF16 is unaffected, since Turing has no BF16 hardware. A user’s variant of the card at 260 W saw a +59% improvement. A separate project, KohakUnlock, on a Leadtek 2080 Ti 22GB saw an 85% improvement on an instruction rate test, with a best matrix-multiply median of +53% against a second, locked card of the same model.There is “not a claim of a 2× application/game speedup,” says KohakUnlock’s README. See Table 2 for a rundown of the numbers for all three generations. The turing-unlock README notes that the mod “may damage your hardware,” while KohakUnlock adds that it “can hang a GPU or host, prevent boot, corrupt data, or damage hardware,” so caution is advised.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Swipe to scroll horizontally Matrix-multiply benchmark gains, unlocked vs. stock Card Precision Gain Tested by RTX 4090 FP16 / BF16 +12–34% / up to +20% One owner, Linux, 450 W RTX 4070 Ti (MSI) FP16 / BF16 +80.1% / +76.4% Separate Windows port, one card RTX 3090 Ti FP16 / BF16 / TF32 +35% / +80% / +94% One user, modified Nvidia driver, 450 W RTX 3090 BF16 +25–67% User reports; lowest at a 225 W cap RTX 3080 10GB BF16 +70–73% User report RTX 3080 20GB mod BF16 +56–59% User reports RTX 3070 BF16 +73–81% User reports RTX 3060 12GB BF16 About +80% User reports RTX 2080 Ti 22GB mod (Dell) FP16 +36–64% turing-unlock developer, 250 W, by matrix size RTX 2080 Ti 22GB mod FP16 +59% One user, 260 W RTX 2080 Ti 22GB mod (Leadtek) FP16 +53% KohakUnlock; best median vs. a locked card RTX 2080 Ti 11GB (ASUS, stock) FP16 +77% haohervchb pre-boot loader How the exploit worksThe explainer for gpu-unlock states that the rate limits are in two “speed selector” registers that the host driver can’t write, but Nvidia’s signed SEC2 “Booter” firmware has a stack buffer overflow which can be exploited to run code in “heavy secure” mode. This was discovered after Nvidia published a debug Booter encrypted with a known public test key. A single 4-byte write with the V67 payload opens the privilege mask so the host can set the full rate, and the module then resets the card before Nvidia’s driver binds it.The underlying bug is described in Jon Pry’s “A Canary in the Crypto Mine: Defeating Stack Protection in a GPU Secure Coprocessor,” published on Zenodo in June. The stack overflow was found on the CMP 170HX in the Heavy Secure Falcon, and the V67 constants come from WildFlash1st/cmp90hx-unlock. The pre-driver timing gpu-unlock uses appear to come from WildFlash1st’s separate Windows EFI bootloader, cmp90hx-unlock-for-windows, while the best-known use of the exploit is the CMP Unlocker for the CMP 170HX. Zagitta, the maintainer of gpu-unlock, said on Hacker News that the project is their work but “the exploits … aren’t my ideas by any means” and that the unlock “just flips the 2 bits” needed.Zagitta said that RTX 40 support is in progress and that forks are already unlocking those cards. Zagitta added that Hopper and Blackwell cards are “out of scope for this approach” at least.The Ada fork says other boards “remain unverified” and that shared firmware “does not establish support for untested cards.” The turing-unlock project, likewise, has a list of untested Turing IDs. Gaps remain for GA103 and most Ada and Turing cards. None of the projects contains a roadmap, but data is being gathered, as gpu-unlock is asking GPU owners for compatibility reports. history.author: Shane Downing
history.titleZh: Nvidia RTX 20、30 和 40 系列 GPU 遭破解，以解除半速 AI 限速
history.descriptionZh:
修改者利用固件漏洞，找到了移除英伟达 GeForce RTX 20、30、40 系列显卡上人为设置的“半速”AI 性能限制的方法。该限制原本使这些消费级 GPU 的 FP32 累加矩阵运算只能以各自 FP16 累加速率的一半运行，而英伟达的 Turing、Ampere 专业卡不受此限制。解锁后，显卡可恢复原生矩阵数学吞吐，从而加快大语言模型的提示处理（prefill）以及图像生成等任务。不过，实际工作负载的收益远低于峰值翻倍，聊天机器人逐 token 生成速度基本不变，因为该阶段主要受显存带宽限制。

目前有三个独立项目提供不同世代的解锁方案，各自提供非官方 Linux 模块，另有实验性 Windows 构建采用不同路径。gpu-unlock 面向 Ampere，列出 GA102/GA103/GA104/GA106 系列 ID，已报告支持 RTX 3090 Ti、3090、3080 10GB、显存改装 3080 20GB、3070、3060 12GB；3070 Ti 和 GA103 卡未测试，一张 RTX 3080 Ti 20GB OEM 卡仍保持半速。gpu-unlock-ada 面向 Ada，覆盖 RTX 4090，并实验性支持 4090 D、4070 Ti Super、4060 Ti 16GB，每类仅一张卡。turing-unlock 改编自 gpu-unlock，适用于 RTX 2080 Ti，其他 Turing GPU 被列为未测试，且因 Turing 不支持 BF16，只能针对 FP16。RTX 50（Blackwell）不在支持范围内，开发者称其超出该方案范围。

性能方面，峰值翻倍主要体现在张量速率上：Ada 分支开发者的 RTX 4090 从 FP16 165.6 TFLOPS 提升到 331.6 TFLOPS，BF16 从 165.5 TFLOPS 提升到 330.6 TFLOPS。但实际矩阵乘法基准中，一位独立用户的 cuBLAS GEMM 中位数仅提升 12%–34%，另一项最高约 20%。一张 Windows 上的 RTX 4070 Ti 取得更大的矩阵乘法提升，分别为 +80.1% 和 +76.4%，差异可能来自功耗限制。RTX 3090 Ti 在修改版英伟达驱动下，FP16 +35%、BF16 +80%、TF32 +94%。gpu-unlock 的 README 汇总用户报告：RTX 3090 的 BF16 矩阵乘法提升 25%–67%，3080 10GB 提升 70%–73%，显存改装 20GB 版提升 56%–59%，3070 提升 73%–81%，3060 12GB 约 +80%，但这些数据并非直接可比。功耗上限“影响很大”：最低的 +25% 来自 225W 功耗上限的卡。Ampere 上，LLM prefill 提升 14%–36%，扩散模型和 FlashAttention 也有加速，但 LLM 解码和 INT8 基本不变。RTX 2080 Ti 22GB 显存改装版中，Dell OEM 卡限制在 250W 时，FP16 矩阵乘法按矩阵尺寸提升 36%–64%；一张 260W 的同类卡提升 59%；KohakUnlock 在一张 Leadtek 2080 Ti 22GB 上测得指令速率提升 85%，矩阵乘法中位数相对同型号锁速卡提升 53%。另有 ASUS 原厂 2080 Ti 11GB 通过预启动加载器取得 +77% 的 FP16 提升。KohakUnlock 明确表示，这并不是宣称应用或游戏能获得 2 倍加速。

技术原理上，gpu-unlock 的说明称，速率限制位于两个主机驱动无法写入的“速度选择”寄存器中，但英伟达签名的 SEC2 “Booter”固件存在栈缓冲区溢出，可被利用在“heavy secure”模式下执行代码。该问题是在英伟达发布一个用已知公共测试密钥加密的调试版 Booter 后被发现的。通过 V67 payload 进行一次 4 字节写入即可打开权限掩码，使主机能够设置全速率；模块随后在英伟达驱动绑定前重置显卡。底层漏洞描述来自 Jon Pry 于 6 月发表在 Zenodo 的论文《A Canary in the Crypto Mine: Defeating Stack Protection in a GPU Secure Coprocessor》，栈溢出是在 CMP 170HX 的 Heavy Secure Falcon 上发现的，V67 常量来自 WildFlash1st/cmp90hx-unlock。gpu-unlock 使用的驱动前时机似乎来自 WildFlash1st 的独立 Windows EFI 启动加载器 cmp90hx-unlock-for-windows，而该漏洞最知名的应用是面向 CMP 170HX 的 CMP Unlocker。gpu-unlock 维护者 Zagitta 在 Hacker News 上表示，项目是其工作，但“这些漏洞利用绝非我的想法”，解锁“只是翻转所需的 2 个比特”。他还称 RTX 40 支持仍在推进，分支已在解锁这些卡；Hopper 和 Blackwell 至少对该方法“超出范围”。

影响与应用场景方面，这一解锁主要有利于本地 AI 工作负载中的矩阵密集型阶段，例如 LLM 提示预填充、扩散图像生成和 FlashAttention 等，对受显存带宽约束的逐 token 解码帮助有限。由于覆盖范围仍不完整，GA103 和大多数 Ada、Turing 卡存在空白，且共享固件并不能证明未测试卡获得支持。风险也不容忽视：turing-unlock 的 README 警告该修改“可能损坏硬件”，KohakUnlock 则称其“可能导致 GPU 或主机挂起、阻止启动、损坏数据或损坏硬件”，因此需要谨慎对待。各项目没有路线图，但正在收集兼容性报告。

history.title: Bitcoin reward offered to anyone who could break into an unpatched server running PHP, hacker cracks site and claims bounty
history.description: The “Steal My Bitcoin” challenge offers a bounty to anyone who can breach a deliberately vulnerable PHP website using the recently disclosed PHP2Shell flaws. The challenge follows previous recoveries of locked Bitcoin fortunes through software vulnerabilities and AI-assisted investigation, but no successful claim has been confirmed.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A hacker has successfully breached a vulnerable server, claiming a prize pot worth $2,021.22 in Bitcoin after exploiting PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, a posting on the Steal My Bitcoin website has shown. The challenge's creator confirmed the win on October 25, ending an experiment designed to test claims that exploiting critical software vulnerabilities is becoming easier.The challenge, hosted on the website a day earlier and announced through a forum post, initially offered approximately $502 worth of Bitcoin. Donations subsequently increased the pot to 0.02511679 BTC, worth $2,021.22 at the time of the win. The creator's website recorded the successful claim at 15:47 UTC on October 25, after the challenge had been running for approximately 19.28 hours.The experiment follows the disclosure of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, two critical PHP vulnerabilities that can allow remote code execution under certain conditions. The flaws received critical severity ratings, and fixes were released on October 21. Turning the vulnerabilities into a reliable attack, however, requires more than simply running a publicly available exploit against an arbitrary server.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The challenge's creator, posting under the name ‘cloudlandsdev’, had said the project was designed to see whether anyone could use the vulnerabilities to compromise the server and claim its Bitcoin. “Made this because I'm curious if anyone out there has figured out how to actually use this PHP RCE, we spent the last few days panicking. Have fun!” the creator wrote.PHP2Shell refers to two vulnerabilities in PHP’s request-handling and memory-management processes. Under vulnerable configurations, an attacker could potentially exploit these flaws to execute code with the privileges of the web server account. You may like OpenAI says ChatGPT Sol helped uncover critical PHP flaws that could affect 70% of websites Hacker turns 25 cents into 46 billion fake Bitcoins to steal $770,000 Hackers drain $320 million in Bitcoin from Liquid Network, emptying roughly 95% of federation wallet The experiment quickly attracted attention, but the resulting traffic also became a problem. In an update, the creator said visitors were exhausting the server's available computing resources shortly after each capacity increase. Limited storage also prevented the server from retaining all its logs, complicating efforts to document a successful attempt.The winner, ‘KillaBoi’, published a proof of concept on GitHub describing the attack against the live challenge and providing a local test environment. The exploit took advantage of PHP's handling of multipart uploads and session data, where, by pushing a PHP worker beyond its memory limit, the attacker could leave internal state in an inconsistent condition. Subsequent requests then exposed memory contents through session cookies, providing information about the locations of PHP's memory structures and executable code.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsNotably, the attacker used those addresses to construct a forged PHP data structure that triggered command execution during cleanup. The final request returned evidence that the command had run inside the PHP process. Although the server was successfully compromised, the recovered private key did not match the advertised prize address. However, on-chain data shows the funds were subsequently sent to an address “bc1qr4…lk7a9”, labeled as a Kraken cold wallet.Bitcoin recovery efforts have previously involved reverse-engineering software rather than exploiting a live server. In 2024, hardware hacker Joe Grand, known as ‘Kingpin”, and researcher Bruno recovered access to 43.6 BTC belonging to an owner identified as Michael, who had forgotten a 20-character wallet password.The researchers reverse-engineered an older version of RoboForm's password generator and identified a flaw that made the password predictable. They recovered the wallet in November 2023, when the Bitcoin was worth approximately $1.6 million. Its value had climbed to nearly $3 million by the time the recovery was reported in May 2024.A more recent case involved a Bitcoin holder who recovered five BTC worth roughly $400,000 in May 2026 after losing access to the wallet for years. The pseudonymous owner, known as ‘cprkrn’, said Anthropic's Claude AI helped identify a backup file from December 2019, which could be decrypted using a password the owner had previously written down in a notebook. The backup contained the keys needed to access the Bitcoin.The latest event comes as security teams face pressure to patch PHP installations following the public disclosure of PHP2Shell. A separate report on the vulnerability disclosure controversy detailed how premature publication disrupted the coordinated release process. That said, for now, evidence of the latest successful attack suggests that exploiting these PHP vulnerabilities may not be that hard after all.
history.author: Newton Gitonga
history.titleZh: 比特币悬赏给任何能入侵运行PHP的未打补丁服务器的人，黑客攻破网站并领取赏金
history.descriptionZh:
一场名为“Steal My Bitcoin”的公开挑战显示，一名黑客成功攻破了一台存在漏洞的服务器，并领取了价值2021.22美元的比特币奖金。挑战创建者于10月25日确认了这次成功，结束了这项旨在检验“利用关键软件漏洞是否正变得越来越容易”的实验。该挑战于一天前上线，并通过论坛帖子公布，最初奖金约为502美元，随后在捐赠推动下增至0.02511679 BTC，获胜时价值2021.22美元。创建者网站记录的成功领取时间为10月25日15:47 UTC，此时挑战已运行约19.28小时。

实验背景是CVE-2026-109618和CVE-2026-109619两个严重PHP漏洞的公开披露。这两个漏洞在特定条件下可导致远程代码执行，均获得严重级别评级，修复程序于10月21日发布。不过，把公开漏洞转化为针对任意服务器的可靠攻击并不简单。挑战创建者“cloudlandsdev”表示，该项目是为了观察是否有人能真正利用这些PHP远程代码执行漏洞攻破服务器并取走比特币，并称团队此前几天一直在为此紧张。所谓“PHP2Shell”涉及PHP请求处理和内存管理过程中的两个漏洞；在易受攻击配置下，攻击者可能以Web服务器账户权限执行代码。

挑战迅速引发关注，但流量也带来问题。创建者称，每次扩容后不久，访问者就会耗尽服务器计算资源；存储限制还导致服务器无法保留全部日志，增加了记录成功攻击过程的难度。获胜者“KillaBoi”在GitHub发布了概念验证，描述了对实时挑战环境的攻击，并提供本地测试环境。该利用方式针对PHP对multipart上传和会话数据的处理：攻击者先将PHP工作进程推过内存限制，使内部状态进入不一致条件；后续请求再通过会话Cookie暴露内存内容，从而泄露PHP内存结构和可执行代码的位置信息。攻击者利用这些地址构造伪造的PHP数据结构，在清理阶段触发命令执行，最终请求返回了命令已在PHP进程内运行的证据。

尽管服务器被成功攻破，但恢复出的私钥与挑战宣传的奖励地址并不匹配。链上数据显示，相关资金随后被发送至地址“bc1qr4…lk7a9”，该地址被标注为Kraken冷钱包。文章还对比了此前的比特币恢复案例：2024年，硬件黑客Joe Grand（“Kingpin”）和研究员Bruno通过逆向旧版RoboForm密码生成器，发现密码可预测缺陷，帮助化名Michael的持有者恢复43.6 BTC；2023年11月恢复时价值约160万美元，2024年5月报道时接近300万美元。2026年5月，化名“cprkrn”的持有者在Anthropic的Claude AI帮助下找到2019年12月的备份文件，并用此前记在笔记本上的密码解密，恢复了约40万美元的5 BTC。

此次事件发生之际，安全团队正因PHP2Shell公开披露而面临修补PHP安装的压力。另一份关于漏洞披露争议的报告称，过早发布扰乱了协调披露流程。就目前而言，这次成功攻击的证据表明，利用这些PHP漏洞可能并没有想象中那么困难。
